domain: daily volume/participation and liquidity-shape information: relative dollar-volume participation shifts across the frozen sector-ETF cohort, with explicit market neutralization

mechanism.causal_story: Sector-ETF dollar-volume participation is the observable daily footprint of reallocating institutional flow. When a sector's recent participation rises sharply relative to its own trailing baseline (a participation shock), the incremental flow is disproportionately allocation- or information-motivated rather than liquidity noise, and ETF-level allocation flows are sticky, so high-participation sectors experience positive relative drift and low-participation sectors negative relative drift over the following quarter. The ranking feature is a volume ratio computed without any price-return term, so the mechanism is a participation-state mechanism, not price momentum and not trend/defensive rotation.
mechanism.why_after_cost_information: The signal is slow: quarterly decision cadence with persistent participation ranks produces an estimated ~3.8/yr two-way turnover, i.e. a ~38 bps/yr base cost drag (10 bps/side, charged once per fill) and ~76 bps/yr at 20 bps stress. The documented volume-shock premium in the single-name literature is measured in percent per month at formation horizons of one month, an order of magnitude above the ETF-level cost drag; the test decides whether the effect survives aggregation to liquid sector ETFs, not whether it exceeds costs by construction.
mechanism.falsifiable_prediction: Sign prediction: the long-minus-short spread (top-3 participation-shock sectors minus bottom-3 participation-shock sectors, dollar-neutral) has positive after-cost expectancy over S0, positive risk-matched excess in at least 2 of 3 folds, and overall incremental alpha > 0 versus the frozen risk-matched SPY context. Equivalently, the cross-sectional rank correlation between the participation-shock ratio and next-quarter sector total returns is positive. A negative spread, alpha <= 0, or reproduction by the stale-rank control falsifies the prediction.

primary_sources: Gervais, S., Kaniel, R., & Mingelgrin, D. H. (2001). The High-Volume Return Premium. Journal of Finance, 56(5), 875-919.
Lo, A. W., & Wang, J. (2000). Trading Volume: Definitions, Data Analysis, and Implications of Portfolio Theory. Review of Financial Studies, 13(2), 271-302.
Lee, C. M. C., & Swaminathan, B. (2000). Price Momentum and Trading Volume. Journal of Finance, 55(5), 2017-2069.

files_and_fields.{SYM}_none_p1.json for each of SPY, XLB,: fields datetime, close, volume (raw as-traded); dollar volume DV_s(u) = close_s(u) * volume_s(u) is a declared price-level feature on the authorized raw path; the volume field of the _all files is NOT used (back-adjustment distorts it)
files_and_fields.{SYM}_all_p1.json for the 11 sector ETFs: fields datetime, close (split+dividend adjusted) for leg and spread total returns
files_and_fields.SPY_all_p1.json: field datetime, close (adjusted) used only as the benchmark context denominator; SPY is never held and never a feature

authorized_pit_inputs.screening_window: S0 2018-04-04..2025-07-31 only (1842 SPY sessions); max scored date <= 2025-07-31; S1 rows never read
authorized_pit_inputs.warmup: 252-session lookback (21 + 231) drawn from the 2076 pre-S0 sessions strictly before 2018-04-04; within the 252-session warmup allowance
authorized_pit_inputs.explicitly_not_used: intraday bars, fundamentals, earnings calendars, borrow/short interest, ETF holdings, institutional flows, options/implied vol, any network or paid data; _none series never used for return computation

universe_and_schedule.universe: the 11 sector ETFs {XLB, XLC, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLRE, XLU, XLV, XLY} ranked at each decision; SPY never traded; fixed availability rule (not performance-based): XLC enters the rank set only from the first decision session where its full 252-session warmup exists (~2019-06, derived deterministically from the snapshot calendar), before that the rank set is the 10 available sectors
universe_and_schedule.decision_clock: per fold, every 63rd SPY session starting at the fold's first scored session (offsets 0, 63, 126, ...), decision computed on that session's PIT close; ~10 decision slots per fold, 30 total across S0
universe_and_schedule.holding_period: 63 sessions per decision book, weights fixed between decision slots; force-flat at every fold boundary per baseline invariants (the final slot of a fold may be truncated)
universe_and_schedule.fill_clock: next allowed session after the decision session, per baseline invariants fill convention (no same-session fill)
universe_and_schedule.book_shape: gross 1.0, net 0.0, cash 1.0; exactly 6 non-CASH legs per decision (3 long, 3 short)

anchor: At decision session t (PIT close): for each eligible sector s, shock_s(t) = mean(DV_s over sessions t-20..t) / mean(DV_s over sessions t-251..t-21) (21-session numerator over its own 231-session prior baseline; 252-session total lookback). Rank eligible sectors by shock descending; ties broken by ticker alphabetical ascending. Long the 3 highest-shock sectors at +1/6 each; short the 3 lowest-shock sectors at -1/6 each; no other legs; weights fixed until the next decision slot; fills at the next allowed session; force-flat at fold boundaries. Single fixed rule; no parameter menu, no vol-scaling, no hysteresis.
neighbour: Same construction as the anchor with one fixed change: the participation numerator uses 63 sessions instead of 21 (shock63_s(t) = mean(DV_s, t-62..t) / mean(DV_s, t-251..t-63); total lookback still 252), same 3v3 dollar-neutral quarterly book, same tie and eligibility rules. This is a fixed single variant probing the tempo of the same mechanism: if the participation-shift premium is real, the slower participation tempo should also carry positive risk-matched spread alpha. Not a lookback rescue of any forbidden family: the family conditions on volume only and has no price-return or trend term.

causal_negative_control.control: Stale-participation control: identical surface form (3v3 dollar-neutral, per-fold quarterly decision slots, 63-session holding, same eligibility and tie rules) but every shock is computed fully stale by exactly one holding period: numerator mean(DV_s, t-83..t-63), denominator mean(DV_s, t-251..t-84). The control trades the same book shape from participation ranks that are one quarter old at the decision clock.
causal_negative_control.must_not_carry_if_causal_story_true: If contemporaneous participation shifts are the causal ingredient, a fully stale rank carries no information about which sectors are currently experiencing participation shocks, and the stale book must not earn spread alpha after costs.
causal_negative_control.preregistered_falsification_rule: The control refutes the mechanism if control after-cost expectancy > 0 AND |control incremental alpha| >= 0.5 x anchor incremental alpha (mirror of the frozen control_alpha_abs_ratio_lt 0.5 gate at anchor scale). Independently, a negative anchor expectancy with a worse control also rejects the anchor family per the frozen negative-result rule.

factor_alpha_test: Per the frozen benchmark contract: incremental alpha = arm return - risk-matched SPY context, where this arm's declared frozen risk-match scale is 0.5 (the long-leg gross exposure of the dollar-neutral book, applied ex ante to the SPY total-return path; realized arm volatility is never substituted post hoc). Evaluated per fold and overall; gates: risk-matched excess positive in >= 2/3 folds and overall incremental alpha > 0. Sector beta is plausible because the legs are sector ETFs, so the authorized equal-weight sector factor is added: daily OLS r_arm = a + b1*r_SPY + b2*r_EW_sector + eps over each fold and over S0; report annualized residualized alpha and both betas. The anchor must retain positive residual alpha after sector-factor neutralization (neither SPY beta nor cohort beta). The anchor's realized SPY beta should be ~0 by construction; a materially nonzero realized beta is itself a design-failure flag. Raw PnL is never accepted as alpha.

costs_and_turnover.cost_schedule: 10 bps per side per fill (base), 20 bps per side (stress rerun), charged exactly once per fill per the frozen no-double-charge invariant
costs_and_turnover.expected_turnover: Frozen convention sum(abs(delta_weight)) over non-CASH legs, annualized two-way. Base case: ~1 leg pair replaced per decision -> 4/6 = 0.67 two-way per decision x ~4.04 decisions/yr ~= 2.7/yr, plus initial build and 3 fold-boundary force-flat rebuilds (4 x 2.0 over 7.24 yr) ~= +1.1/yr -> ~3.8/yr two-way.
costs_and_turnover.why_inside_ceiling: Base estimate ~3.8/yr sits inside the frozen 6.0 two-way/yr ceiling with ~35% headroom because quarterly participation ranks are persistent (the denominator changes slowly, so leg membership churns by ~1 leg per side per decision, not wholesale). Adverse case (2+2 legs replaced at every decision) computes to ~6.4/yr and would breach the ceiling; that outcome is preregistered as an accepted falsification surface of the arm, not a parameter to tune.
costs_and_turnover.cost_drag: ~38 bps/yr base, ~76 bps/yr at stress; the hypothesized quarterly participation premium must clear this drag after costs, which is exactly what the after-cost expectancy and PF gates test.

sample_size_floor: ~10 decision periods per fold (63-session cadence over fold spans of ~607-619 sessions, offsets 0..567) and 30 total scheduled across S0; meets the frozen floors (>=5 per fold, >=30 total) exactly, with zero slack: if any slot is voided (data halt, calendar anomaly) the arm falls below the floor and is scored ineligible rather than re-timed. Profit factor is computed over the 30 decision-level PnLs under the frozen position-PF convention; the sample is thin but per contract.
drop_one_design: Drop-one-ETF: rerun the full book excluding the single max-contribution symbol by cumulative PnL; the remaining 9-10 sectors are re-ranked from scratch under the identical rule (book still 3v3, members may change), so survival requires the mechanism to survive the loss of its single best leg rather than mere deletion of one position. This stays meaningful because rank churn rotates sector membership across periods, so no single ETF can dominate by construction, and the frozen 35% ETF positive-PnL-share gate is enforced ex post. Drop-one-fold: min over folds of expectancy with that fold removed; survival requires min > 0; with ~10 decisions per fold, any single-fold concentration also trips the frozen fold-positive-share <= 0.5 gate.
failure_interpretation: A reject (after-cost expectancy <= 0, incremental alpha <= 0, stale-rank control reproduction, turnover ceiling breach, or drop-one failure) means: relative dollar-volume participation at sector-ETF granularity carries no after-cost quarterly-horizon information beyond market and cohort beta. The Gervais-style volume-shock premium does not survive aggregation from single names to liquid sector ETFs at daily-data granularity, and the participation-shift-ranking mechanism class is closed for this data universe and horizon. It would not license rescue variants (other lookbacks, other leg counts, vol-scaling, trend overlays), which are pre-declared ineligible under the plan's anti-rescue rule.
source_to_test_map: 1. Gervais, Kaniel & Mingelgrin (2001) form volume shocks as recent volume relative to a trailing own baseline and show top-vs-bottom volume portfolios earn a premium -> implementation steps: (i) compute DV_s(u) from raw close x volume; (ii) shock_s(t) = 21-session mean / 231-session prior mean; (iii) long top-3 / short bottom-3 rank book at quarterly cadence.

2. Lo & Wang (2000) model volume as a state variable with cross-sectional pricing content -> implementation steps: (iv) participation used as a standing state, traded as a dollar-neutral spread; (v) explicit market neutralization via frozen risk-match scale 0.5 and SPY + EW-sector factor OLS.

3. Lee & Swaminathan (2000) show volume carries information distinct from price momentum -> implementation step: (vi) the ranking feature contains no price-return term; a feature-correlation check of shock_s against trailing 12-1 sector returns is reported (not tuned) at implementation time so A7-N can verify the anchor is not a momentum descendant.

implementation_estimate.breakdown: 0.5d snapshot loader + fold-offset scheduler reuse; 0.5d dollar-volume/shock feature with hand-computed golden fixtures; 1.0d quarterly rank-book executor (fold force-flat, next-allowed-session fills, cost-once, frozen turnover convention); 1.0d control and neighbour arm variants plus PIT/no-lookahead mutation tests and accounting invariants
implementation_estimate.risk_notes: XLC warmup availability branch must be deterministic from the snapshot calendar; the per-fold offset scheduler must be byte-reproducible; PIT guard that every shock window ends at the decision session with no lookahead; turnover must be measured under the single frozen convention; resource risk is minimal (12 symbols, ~1842 S0 sessions, one scored arm serial).

outcome_blind_attestation.statement: I did not read per-arm V2/V3 outcomes; this proposal was written before any V4 scoring
